**⚠⚠ THE THIRTY-SEVEN RULES:** 1. CLAMP AT SELECTION (§29e/§46/§53/§56.4). 2. NEVER PATCH `TryRebuildDirtyRegionsAndRooms` (§29c). 3. REGION CONNECTIVITY IS MORE OPTIMISTIC THAN THE PATHFINDER: flood CELLS. 4. ON WHAT IS ON THE MAP. 8 (§52.6): A LOAD-TIME REPAIR PASS MUST NEVER RE-CREATE WHAT THE PLAYER DELIBERATELY REMOVED. 9 (§53): SOME MISPLACEMENTS ARE NOT VISIBLE IN THE CELL. 10 (§54): A STRUCTURE IS WATCH BEING WRITTEN. 14 (§56m): BEFORE RELOCATING DATA, ASK WHAT IS ALREADY AT THE DESTINATION. 15 (§57i): ASSERT ALWAYS, NARRATE ON REQUEST. 16 (§56o): COUNT THE FOREIGN MOD'S WRITE PATHS. 17 (§56q): A PASSING RUN THAT DID NOT REPRODUCE THE FAILURE IS NOT A FIX. 18 (§57a): NEVER EXONERATE A SUSPECT ON ONE CLEAN SAMPLE. 19 (§57f): **`TicksGame` RESTARTS AT 0 EVERY NEW GAME.** 20 (§57g): MOVING WORK (§61f): **EVERY READ OF THE MAP THE PLAYER CAN REACH MUST PASS THE SAME "IS IT DRAWN" GATE THE RENDERER USES.** 27 (§62c): **PREFER THE OPERATION EVERY HOST IS ALREADY FORCED TO HANDLE (SPAWN/DESPAWN) OVER THE ONE EACH HOST HANDLES ITS OWN WAY (FLICK).** 28 (§63a): **A PERMANENT FICTION INSTALLED FOR ONE SUBSYSTEM IS READ AS FACT BY EVERY OTHER ONE.** 29 (§0b): **REPORT OUTCOMES, NOT INTENTIONS.** 30 (§66d): **A FELT DURATION IS A CHAIN, NOT A NUMBER.** 31 (§66f): **WHEN A GUARDED HANDOFF FAILS IN THE FIELD, MAKE THE GUARD SAY WHICH CLAUSE DECLINED.** 32 (§69a): **TURNING OFF A TICK TURNS OFF EVERY SERVICE THAT RODE ON IT.** 33 (§62k): **A FILTER THAT CAN REJECT EVERYTHING MUST SAY SO - `work=0 | skip:(none)` IS A CONTRADICTION, NOT A CLEAN RUN.** 34 (§62l): **AN INVISIBLE THING IS ABSENT FROM EVERY SECTION LAYER, NOT JUST THE MAP MESH - `DrawerType.None` IS FILTERED IN `SectionLayer_Things.Regenerate`, SO IT CAN NEVER APPEAR IN AN OVERLAY EITHER. Corollary: the map mesh and each overlay are SEPARATE METHODS, so one can be suppressed without the other.** 35 (§62n): **MAKING A CLONED FOREIGN DEF VISIBLE ENTERS IT INTO EVERY FOREIGN LOOKUP THE HOST BUILT FROM ITS OWN AUTHORED LISTS - AND IT IS IN NONE OF THEM.** 36 (§70a): **WHEN WE SPAWN SOMETHING VANILLA NORMALLY SPAWNS, WE MUST RUN VANILLA'S OWN LEGALITY PREDICATE, NOT A SUMMARY OF IT. A hand-rolled approximation of `CanEverPlantAt` silently dropped `wildTerrainTags`, and the failure mode was not an error but a slow death with no log line anywhere. Corollary: prefer the predicate that TAKES THE CELL over re-deriving its clauses.** 37 (§71a): **NAME THE ENFORCEMENT POINT BEFORE NAMING THE SYMPTOM. Plant illegality has TWO with opposite outcomes: spawned-onto-bad-terrain = slow silent death (§70); terrain-changed-under-plant = INSTANT silent `Destroy()` in `TerrainGrid.DoTerrainChangedEffects`. I published the wrong symptom into a triage note for a day because I predicted from the def data without walking the SetTerrain path. Corollary of rule 36's spirit: read the engine's own handler for the transition you are predicting.**

# 62. UTILITY COLUMN REWORK — ✅ SHIPPED (window 7). Columns user-verified run #277; §62.J/.M shipped unverified and §62.J turned out to be half-broken on VE pipes (§62.N).

**DESIGN (user-locked):** 4 typed columns, MERGE ONLY (metering permanently declined; "one inter-connected base"), per-network disconnect gizmos, one level per column (stack for more), research Electricity + Machining, flat cost Steel 60 + Comp 2, HARD DELETE of risers (no converter; user chose this).

**62.A TYPES:** POWER, PIPE (all fluids AND gases), CLIMATE, DATA. **62.B CLASSIFIER:** forcedType → id=="Power" → keywords on id+template defName+label, ORDER Power / Data / Climate → default Pipe. ⚠ "cool" NOT "cold". ⚠ NO "gas" keyword. ⚠ NEVER classify on `resource.unit` (Helixien GAS declares `l`). FIELD-VERIFIED 9/9 correct.
**62.C BUILDING** (`Building_ABColumn`): vanilla-Column-shaped (holdsRoof, PassThroughOnly, fill 0.25, Structure). AUTO-CONNECT on first construction, `autoEnabled` scribed (rule 8). Toggle = spawn/despawn carrier pair (rule 27). ⚠ STACKS SHARE CARRIERS: claimants = column IN the cell + column one Slot BELOW. ⚠ Carriers destroyable=false: DeSpawn only.
**62.D LINK** (`ABColumnLink`): partner = same `ABCarrierExt.network` at cell ± Slot; spawned == live.
**62.E DELETED:** 30 riser defs, root Compat/, 90 riser PNGs, CompABRiserSwitch, PlaceWorker_ABOnWall, ABDevTools.V2Risers, Building_ABPowerBreaker, PokeRebuild, LoadFolders gates.
**62.F ART:** user-generated via Nano Banana Pro, 4 files, 1200x896 RGBA; originals in `.modmixer/art-src/`. ⚠ drawSize x MUST stay 1.34*y ((1.61,1.2) + z offset 0.18).
**62.G CARRIER GEN:** probes + `ABColumnAdapterDef` escape hatch → clone host conduit → carrier def at `GenerateImpliedDefs_PreResolve`, `AddImpliedDef` PINNED to ThingDef. FIELD-VERIFIED: 9 networks, 9 carriers, 0 skipped, every template a plain conduit.
**62.H DATA ADAPTERS:** RimIOT = postfix on `RebuildAllNetworks`, merge-by-removal member by member, winner caches rebuilt via the host's own surface. ⚠ Safe because its 500-tick audits are MEMBER-based not spatial. Eccentric = postfix `InitConduit` calling their private `MergeNetworks`, plus postfix `DeregisterConduit` setting `dirty=true` because their cardinal-only split CANNOT dissolve a cross-band union.
**62.I ROOF:** `holdsRoof` means "can SUPPORT a roof", never "makes one". A column in the open had none, so `ABSkySync.Resolve` fell to `AB_WallTop` - buildable but IMPASSABLE. Fix: lay a REAL `RoofConstructed` on the column's own cell (§45's recipe, as `Building_ABStairs2` does), so `Patch_RoofGrid_ABSyncAbove` re-derives the cell above as walkable `AB_RoofSurface`. `roofPlaced` scribed; DeSpawn takes back only our own roof (rule 8); existing roofs never overwritten.
**62.J VISIBLE CARRIERS:** dropped slice 1's forced `DrawerType.None` (its comment about gutter cells was stale - carriers live in band cells). One field fixed two requests: columns appear in network overlays, AND the up-cell carrier IS the visible "conduit on the floor above" with no second def and no auto-construction to balance. Linking survives the clone (`graphicData.linkFlags`, not defName) - **for hosts that resolve art from the def. VEF PipeSystem does not: see §62.N.**
**62.M HIDE UNDER COLUMN** (`Patch_SectionLayer_ABHideCarrierUnderColumn`): §62.J's cost was pipe/wire stubs poking out from under the column art. A carrier sharing a cell with a `Building_ABColumn` skips printing to the GENERAL layer only. ⚠ The map mesh (`SectionLayer_ThingsGeneral.TakePrintFrom` → `Thing.Print`) and the power overlay (`SectionLayer_ThingsPowerGrid.TakePrintFrom` → `PrintForPowerGrid` → `CompPrintForPowerGrid`) are DIFFERENT METHODS, so suppressing one leaves every overlay untouched - including each pipe mod's own layer class. Patching `Thing.Print` would have been broader AND still missed the power overlay. Condition is "a column stands here", which self-maintains for stacks. `ABColumnNetworks.IsCarrier` is a HashSet for the render hot path.
**62.K DBH PREFIX MISMATCH = RULE 33:** the riser era authored ids as "DBH.Sewage" so `Hosts` carried the literal "DBH."; §62's probe builds ids from the NAMESPACE ("DubsBadHygiene.Sewage"), so the filter rejected everything before reaching any decline point. Rimefeller/Rimatomics survived only because their namespace equals the old literal. Fix: prefix DERIVED (`compName.Split('.')[0] + "."`), plus narration for "no id matched" and "matched but no carrier".
**62.L TELEMETRY:** `AB2: network scan` (Debug Actions MENU) prints every network with type/probe/template/carrier/research, MERGE COUNTERS one row per family each with a lastSkip clause, **HOST ART BINDING (§62.N)**, then COLUMNS ON THIS MAP: per column its band, type, roof state, up-cell + terrain, enabled networks, `carrierHere`/`carrierAbove`. ⚠ Power had NO counters through the first field test, which made "the lamp upstairs is dark" unfalsifiable; that gap is why rule 33 exists.

**62.N HOST ART BINDING - FIELD BUG, FIXED, SHIPS THIS PUBLISH FIELD-UNVERIFIED** (`ABPipeGraphics` in `Source/Compat/PipeSystemCompat.cs`). Reported from the field as three lines, one per VE network on one column cell: `Exception printing AB_Carrier_VEF_VNPE_NutrientPasteNet2459388 at (90, 0, 293): KeyNotFoundException: The given key 'AB_Carrier_VEF_VNPE_NutrientPasteNet' was not present in the dictionary` → `PipeSystem.LinkedPipes.GetPipeFor` → `PipeSystem.Building_Pipe.get_Graphic`.

*Cause.* `Building_Pipe.Graphic` is nothing but `LinkedPipes.GetPipeFor(def)`, an unguarded `Dictionary<ThingDef, Graphic_LinkedPipe>` lookup. That dictionary is built once in a `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]` cctor by walking every `PipeNetDef.pipeDefs` - the AUTHORED list. Our carriers are runtime clones and are in no authored list. The bug was DORMANT until §62.J: while carriers were `DrawerType.None` nothing ever asked one for a Graphic. The spam comes from the UP-CELL carrier, because §62.M suppresses the one under the column and the cell above has no column in it.

*Fix.* One dictionary write per carrier, into the host's registry, mapping our carrier to the graphic the host ALREADY built for the template we cloned. Not an approximation - the same object: RimWorld shares one Graphic per def, and both behaviours of a pipe graphic take the THING as an argument (`ShouldLinkWith` asks the map's PipeNetManager whether a net of that resource is at the neighbour cell, so a carrier links into real pipe runs on either band; `Print` is handed the thing to position from).

⚠ **REJECTED THE TIDIER FIX** (adding the carrier to `PipeNetDef.pipeDefs` and letting the framework build the entry): that list is also the authority for `Designator_DeconstructPipe.CanDesignateThing`, so a carrier in it becomes drag-deconstructible - on a `destroyable=false` thing whose `Destroy()` logs an error - and their cctor reads `def.graphic.data.texPath` off everything in the list, inside a foreign cctor, where one unresolved graphic would throw a `TypeInitializationException` and kill pipe art for EVERY net in the game. Rule 14.

⚠ **TIMING RULED OUT THE OBVIOUS HOOK.** The registry is only guaranteed full after `StaticConstructorOnStartupUtility.CallAll`, and we cannot postfix CallAll: `HarmonyBoot` is itself `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]`, so our patches are installed BY that call, mid-flight, and patching a method already on the stack does not affect the running invocation. `RuntimeHelpers.RunClassConstructor` is the answer - idempotent, and forcing it from inside CallAll runs it in the exact phase it would have run in anyway (checked against `PlayDataLoader.DoPlayLoad`: def graphics resolve in an `ExecuteWhenFinished` callback queued before the one that calls CallAll). Also re-run at game start via `[ABGameReset(60)]`, idempotent.

⚠ **THE SELECTOR IS THE HOST'S OWN ANSWER, NOT OUR PROBE NAME:** "is the template a key in their registry" also catches an adapter-def network whose template happens to be a PipeSystem pipe. The object-keyed `IDictionary` indexer returns null for a missing key instead of throwing - unlike the generic one that caused this bug. Rule 33 narration: `PipeSystem: bound=N already=N skippedNonVE=N | skip: …`, and `bound=0` with VE networks detected logs a warning instead of passing silently.

⚠ **WHY THE OTHER FAMILIES SURVIVED:** PipeSystem's OTHER def-keyed cache (`CachedResourceThings`) is built by walking `DefDatabase<ThingDef>.AllDefsListForReading` with `TryGetValue`, so it picked our carriers up for free - which is why connection, merging and `GetNetTransmitter` all worked while only the ART was missing. Generalization is rule 35 and ledger 20.

# 70. BAND FLORA LEGALITY - FIELD BUG, FIXED, SHIPS THIS PUBLISH FIELD-UNVERIFIED (`Source/V2/ABBandFlora.cs`, new; callers `ABCavernGen` step 6 and `ABSkyBandGen.SeedFlora`)

*Report.* With Biomes! Caverns and its dependencies, "most fungi trees and some other plants are dying from the start… some should be spawned only on marsh and marshy soil, but there seems to be a lack of those, and spawned on usual soil they die."

*Cause - one hole, three symptoms.* Both band seeders gated a candidate on nothing but `plant.fertilityMin > terrain.fertility` and then spawned it. Vanilla never does that: `WildPlantSpawner.CalculatePlantsWhichCanGrowAt` runs every candidate through `PlantUtility.CanEverPlantAt`, which ALSO enforces `plant.wildTerrainTags`, `plant.terrainBlacklist`, `completelyIgnoreFertility` and pollution.
1. **The deaths.** Biomes! Core patches tags onto vanilla terrain (`Soil`→`SoilBasic`, `SoilRich`→`SoilRich`, `MarshyTerrain`→`MarshySoil`, `Mud`→`Mud`, `Marsh`→`WaterMarshy`) and Biomes! Caverns gates its flora on them. `BMT_FlakespireFungus` - the fungal TREE and the biome's second most common plant at commonality 2.0 - requires `SoilBasic|SoilRich`, so every one that landed on `MarshyTerrain` (about a fifth of the carve) started dying. `BMT_NuitaeMarsh`/`WrinklecapMarsh`/`NogtylMarsh` require `MarshySoil` only, so nearly all of them started dying on plain `Soil`. `Plant.DyingBecauseOfTerrainTags` → `CurrentDyingDamagePerTick` 0.005 → dead in a few in-game hours, **with no error, no exception and no log line anywhere**.
2. **The "lack of marsh".** The terrain WAS being painted correctly (we drive the biome's own `terrainPatchMakers` exactly as `GenStep_Terrain` does; `TerrainAt` self-initialises per map). But `Mud` and `Marsh` both have **fertility 0**, and our `fertility <= 0.01 → skip` gate discarded them wholesale. So the genuinely wet ground got no plants at all while the species that wanted it were dumped on dry soil - which reads exactly as "there is no marsh".
3. **Thinning.** The old loop drew one plant at random and, if illegal, abandoned the CELL. Mixed terrain therefore came out below the density setting.

*Fix.* `ABFloraPicker`: per-biome pool, terrain-keyed candidate cache (the tag / blacklist / fertility clauses are terrain-only, so they are answered once per `TerrainDef` rather than once per cell), weighted draw from the legal set, then the real `CanEverPlantAt` as the last word before spawning. `FertilityWeightOn` reproduces vanilla's `GetBaseDesiredPlantsCountAt` shape including the **0.1 water floor** when the biome has anything with `completelyIgnoreFertility` - that is what puts nuitae and wrinklecap into `Marsh`.

⚠ **`Mud` STAYING BARE IS CORRECT.** Mud has fertility 0 and is NOT tagged `Water`, so vanilla's own water floor does not reach it and vanilla leaves mud bare on swamp maps too. Parity, not an oversight. Do not "fix" it.

⚠ **THE MAP-TEMPERATURE CLAUSE IS A TOTAL-REJECTION RISK (rule 33).** `CanEverPlantAt` compares the plant's growth range against `map.TileInfo` Min/MaxTemperature - the SURFACE tile's weather, which is meaningless for a sealed basement. On a cold tile it can reject the entire cavern flora and hand back a barren level silently. So a strict pool that comes out EMPTY is rebuilt without that clause and the relaxation is ANNOUNCED (`temperature gate relaxed`), and the same flag is passed through to the per-cell check so a relaxed picker stays relaxed at the point of spawn.

⚠ **SCRATCH BUFFER IS PER-INSTANCE, NOT STATIC.** Two bands can be seeded inside one generation pass; a shared draw buffer would let one band's rejected draws leak into the other's list (§57f statics discipline).

## 70.B CAVERN REGROWTH - OPEN, PRICED, NOT STARTED (ledger 5b)

Found while fixing §70; **not** what was reported, and deliberately not bundled because the first estimate ("route the roof check through `wildPlantsAreCavePlants`") turned out to be wrong.

*Symptom.* Our bands are roofed `RoofRockThick`, which is `isNatural`, so `WildPlantSpawner.GoodRoofForCavePlant` is TRUE for every basement cell. That makes vanilla draw regrowth from the GLOBAL `allCavePlants` list (`cavePlant && cavePlantWeight > 0`) at MTB 130 days and half density. **Every Biomes! Caverns plant is authored `cavePlantWeight 0`**, so none of them are in that list. A fungal-forest basement will therefore drift toward vanilla glowstool over many in-game years.

*Why real Biomes! Caverns maps do not have this problem.* Their cavern maps leave the open cave FLOOR unroofed (only solid rock carries `BMT_RockRoofStable`), so `GoodRoofForCavePlant` is false and the spawner uses the biome's own list. Their only spawner patch is a prefix on `WildPlantSpawnerTickInternal` that swaps the tick loop; they do not touch the plant-choice path.

*What a fix actually costs - three coupled patches, none sufficient alone:*
- **A.** Postfix the `cachedPlantCommonalities` build so band-biome plants get entries. It is built from `map.Biomes`, which for us is the SURFACE biome only, so every band plant currently weighs 0. Cell-free and legitimate (those plants really are on this map).
- **B.** Postfix `GetCommonalityOfPlant`, which short-circuits `cavePlant` plants to `cavePlantWeight` unless `map.Biome.wildPlantsAreCavePlants` - and `map.Biome` is the surface. ⚠ It takes NO cell, so it must be answered at MAP level ("is this plant in a band biome that sets `wildPlantsAreCavePlants`"), never with an ambient current-cell latch. That would be exactly the design ABBandBiome's header rejects.
- **C.** Transpile the `GoodRoofForCavePlant(c)` call inside `CheckSpawnWildPlantAt` that feeds the local `cavePlants`. ⚠ It CANNOT be a postfix on `GoodRoofForCavePlant` itself: `CanRegrowAt` calls the same predicate with the OPPOSITE polarity (roofed cells regrow only when it is true), so flipping it globally stops the basement regrowing anything at all.

⚠ **DO NOT SHIP A PARTIAL.** C without A+B makes the spawner draw from the band list with all-zero weights, `TryRandomElementByWeight` returns false, and regrowth stops entirely - strictly worse than the current glowstool drift.

*Knock-on to weigh before starting:* A makes `AllWildPlants` and `PlantsCommonalitiesSum` include band plants, which shifts SURFACE cluster maths; and `GetDesiredPlantsCountAt`/`SaturatedAt` are already whole-map counters that pit surface plants against basement targets (related to the §60 area-linear audit, ledger 14).

# 71. SMOOTH TERRAIN / NANAME FLOORS - RESOLVED (window 8). BASELINE COMPATIBLE UNMODIFIED AND USER-VERIFIED IN GAME (smoothed bands incl. sky plateau, clean seams, no errors, isolated session with both mods). UPSTREAM REPORT DRAFTED, AWAITING USER PASTE (ledger 5c). NO CODE SHIPPED. Mechanism CORRECTED after first recording (rule 37).

**The mods.** `ChaoticEnrico.SmoothTerrain` (workshop 3502765685, dll under `1.6/Assemblies/` - the registry's dll flag misses versioned folders) rides on `oels.nanamefloors` (NANAME Floors, 3293767181, shaders + `BlendedTerrainDef`). Both ACTIVE in the user's real list. Mechanism: at startup, Smooth Terrain pre-generates 4 rotations of `BlendedTerrainDef` per terrain pair - pairs from `settings.autoDetectDuos` (all `natural || IsWater` terrains, `IsWater` = `HasTag("Water")`) or a curated default list. A postfix on `MapGenerator.GenerateMap` then walks EVERY cell, matches 4 inside-corner patterns against the 8-neighbourhood (3 consecutive foreign neighbours + 2 cardinal base), and REPLACES the centre cell's terrain with the pre-generated blend. No live SetTerrain patch; their mod-settings page has manual "Smooth current map" / "Un-smooth" buttons for live maps.

**Why the baseline works - three structural facts, no code needed:**
1. **Generation ORDER is guaranteed by nesting, not by patch priority.** Our carve runs in the `GenerateContentsIntoMap` postfix, INSIDE `GenerateMap`; their smoothing postfixes `GenerateMap` itself. So they always see the fully-carved banded map: cavern basements and sky plateaus get smoothed at generation, like any vanilla map. (Our degraded slow-path - carve in the GenerateMap postfix when the inner hook missed - has undefined order vs theirs and would leave bands unsmoothed; that path already logs a complaint and is not worth building for.)
2. **Every synthetic terrain of ours is structurally inert to blending.** `AB_OpenAir` (gutters + sky void), `AB_RoofSurface`, `AB_WallTop`, `AB_MountainTop`: none is `natural`, none has the `Water` tag → never in the duo list → no blend def exists for any pair containing them. Their pattern detector can MATCH such a pair (e.g. band-edge cell with gutter neighbours) but the def lookup returns null and the cell is skipped silently. So: no impassable blend can ever appear at a band edge (their `ValidateAndHardenDef` sets `passability = max` of the pair - the hazard that made this survey worth doing), and nothing ever fights ABSkySync's derived-terrain writes.
3. **Whole-map operations stay safe.** Blends inside unopened solid-rock basements (rough-stone vein corners) are cosmetic and mostly overwritten by later mining/carving - identical to what their mod does under vanilla mountains. "Un-smooth" only touches `BlendedTerrainDef` cells (never ours) and pays one `RegenerateEverythingNow` - their button, their cost. Wealth: their gen postfix calls vanilla `WealthWatcher.ResetStaticData` via a reflective wrapper; nothing band-specific.

**⚠ THE ONE REAL INTERACTION (CORRECTED - rule 37; not band-specific, we just host dense tag-gated flora): blends LOSE terrain `tags` from one side, and vanilla INSTANTLY DELETES mismatched plants on the swapped cells.** NANAME's `BlendInner` copies fields by reflection: floats/ints average, but every REFERENCE field not special-cased - including `tags` - comes **from the cover terrain only** (the lower-`renderPrecedence` of the pair, fixed at pre-generation). Fertility is special-cased to `min`. Smooth Terrain's hardening unions `affordances` and maxes `passability` but never touches `tags`. Consequence: `ApplySmoothing` → `SetTerrain` → vanilla `TerrainGrid.DoTerrainChangedEffects` `Destroy()`s on the spot any plant whose `wildTerrainTags` no longer overlap the blend's tags, or whose `fertilityMin` exceeds the min'd fertility (unless `completelyIgnoreFertility`). NOT the §70 slow death - first recording predicted the wrong enforcement point from def data without walking the SetTerrain path (rule 37; user lore saved, things topic). Observable: thinned/bare terrain-corner cells (label "X and Y"), permanent regrowth ineligibility for those species there, and live plants popping if the player presses "Smooth current map". At gen the deletions happen before first render, so players just see slightly barer corners. ⚠ Reproduces WITHOUT us: Core's `Plants_Wild_Swamp.xml` and Odyssey's `Plants_Water.xml` are tag-gated vanilla content.

**Resolution: option (a) chosen by user ("Build A").** Report at `docs/UPSTREAM_SmoothTerrain.md` (paste-ready for workshop 3502765685; suggests a `tags` union in `ValidateAndHardenDef` parallel to their `affordances` union, with the `IsWater = HasTag("Water")` caution). Option (b) - our own guard postfix reverting blends under plants they would kill - REJECTED as a foreign-pair workaround and maintenance liability; revisit only if upstream declines AND a user reports visible flora loss. A "Verified: Smooth Terrain" note ships in this window's change notes.

⚠ **Blend-def population note (rule 4):** auto-detect with a large modlist can mint thousands of runtime TerrainDefs (their own UI warns at 4000). Our per-`TerrainDef` caches (ABFloraPicker) are lazy and only pay for terrains actually encountered, so no action - but any future whole-`DefDatabase<TerrainDef>` walk we add should remember this population exists.
